newsitem.title: UK: S&P rating upgrade boosts Brady trade, Latam prices.
newsitem.headline: S&P rating upgrade boosts Brady trade, Latam prices.

text.p: Brady bond market trade picked up significantly on Wednesday following positive credit rating news for Latin America, dealers said.
"There has been significant buy-side interest in the Latin accounts across-the-board, but I think it was a bit of an over-reaction to the Argentina news," a trader said.

Standard and Poor's said it revised a policy to allow certain issuers in so-called dollarised economies -- where currencies are closely pegged to the U.S. dollar -- to enjoy a higher rating than the sovereign ceiling.
In conjunction with this, S&P raised the foreign currency counterparty ratings of five Argentine financial institutions.

The criteria calls for foreign currency ratings to rise to the level of a counterparty's local currency rating, given the reduced likelihood of government imposed exchange controls in economies where the local currency is widely replaced by hard currencies as the store of value.
S&P also raised its foreign currency corporate credit ratings and debt ratings on certain Argentine corporate issuers.

"This has extremely important implications for Latin America," another dealer said. "So on the back of this news obviously Argentine debt rallied and Brazil was also boosted." Argentina PARS FRBS and DISCs were up 1/16, 3/8 and 1/16 respectively at 1318 GMT.
He said there had been some profit-taking on Argentine Eurobonds.
Brazil C bonds were up 1/8 at 74-7/8 bid.
Peru continued firm following the gains on the postivie news of the hostage rescue. Peru PDI were bid at 59-1/2, up 1-1/4 at 1318 GMT.
Amid the focus on Latin America, dealers said all was quiet on the Eastern European front.
